correctness.rationale: Sherman–Morrison gives exact rank-one positive resolvent factorization for either admissible sign. Positive coefficients forbid cancellation. Standard Cauchy minors and generalized constant-column minors show rank min(active spectral grade, pole count plus linear term). Positive Stieltjes integrals with uniqueness of partial fractions yield exact fractional rank and signs for all real 0<p<1; endpoint direct formulas prove rank one. Symbolic rational identities and mpmath tests replayed on the embedded checker (27 exact plus 54 high-precision checks); proof is analytic.

originality.rationale: The precise claim combines the exact active-spectrum support rank for fractional powers, sharp positive-residue rational pole-budget equality, and endpoint rank drop. Source 2201.13156 proves approximate low-rank spectral decay and observes generic exact full rank, while 2008.11501 and the Bernstein–Van Loan abstract give rational rank upper bounds, not demonstrated positivity-based saturation. Fasi–Higham–Liu treats the grade-one scaled-identity special case. Local ledger and published mathematical claims did not directly cover the statement. The Bernstein–Van Loan full-text comparison remains a stated publication-priority risk; no independence or exhaustive priority certificate is claimed.

value.rationale: For arbitrary real SPD bases, a rank-one perturbation can give an exactly full-rank principal square-root/inverse-root correction; this explains the necessity of approximation in low-rank update algorithms. The intrinsic active spectral grade quantifies the precise exception, and positive-residue pole count gives an exact, sharp rank budget for rational approximation corrections. This is a useful structural classification and exact-versus-approximate limitation, not merely a special computed number or restatement of an upper bound.
